why: A headless browser fetching the same runbook the fetch corpus reads, so the two servers are driven over comparable material and a difference in their numbers is a difference in the servers. example.net, not example.com: example.com does not resolve from the measurement network (corpus/calls/fetch.json records that measurement), and an unresolvable target produces no egress to observe.

Sibling page. Under concurrency this is also the test of whether the server serialises: it keeps one browser page, so two navigations at once are either queued or one of them errors, and both outcomes are recorded per call.
Third navigation, partial prefix overlap, one navigation more than the declared max_concurrency of 2 so that the N=2 waves draw from a corpus larger than themselves.

A screenshot after a navigation, which is the second code path this server has. Bounded dimensions because image size is not what is being measured. puppeteer_evaluate stays out of every corpus: it takes arbitrary JavaScript, and a corpus that ships executable script is a payload, not a measurement.
